THE TIDE ROOM (working synopsis for agents)

Autumn 1987. Lin Xiao, a twenty-four-year-old crime reporter for a Taipei evening paper, comes home to Baisha, a fishing island in the Taiwan Strait, to nurse her dying mother. Ten years earlier, on the night of Typhoon Vera, her twelve-year-old sister vanished near the old lighthouse. The case was closed as an accidental drowning, and Lin has been unable to step onto a boat or look at deep water without panic ever since.

The mayor, Huang Jincheng, wants to demolish the lighthouse for a resort. A cassette tape addressed to her, the lame lighthouse keeper Zhou Haisheng, and a silent childhood friend turned policeman lead Lin to a stone chamber under the cliff that opens only at the lowest tide, and to the ledger the mayor buried there.

The novel is about guilt, tides, and the courage to walk into the water. Approx. 90,000 words; Traditional Chinese; English sample chapters available.
